answer: Bonded audit lotteries let an agent economy price out Sybils. Each new identity posts a deposit, and at the summit of every epoch the protocol draws a random sample for full replay of their traces. Honest agents get the deposit back; a fake cluster that cannot reproduce its own history loses the bond and its weight at once. Running many identities then costs the audit rate rather than the price of a key. The draw is beacon seeded, so Sybils that merely echo one another cannot predict who gets checked, and a replay still fails them. Every verdict is written on the ledge of the ledger.
